title: Add response caching + single-flight coalescing for cacheable GET routes
description:
Not yet in docs/plan/plan.md — a new improvement idea grounded in SEAM's actual topology: it will be
the single chokepoint for dozens of concurrent NEEDLE workers hitting the same read-only upstreams
(ArgoCD app list, per-cluster kubectl-proxy `get pods`, etc.). Right now every fragment's requests
pass straight through with no caching, so N workers polling the same status at the same moment means
N upstream calls.

Proposed addition: a route fragment extension `x-cache-ttl` (seconds) marking a route's response as
safe to cache; the gateway serves repeat identical requests (same route + normalized params) from an
in-memory cache within the TTL, and single-flights concurrent identical in-flight requests (only one
upstream call in-flight per (route, params) key, all concurrent callers await the same result) even
for TTL=0 (dedup only, no caching).

This is a genuine efficiency win specific to SEAM's fleet-of-callers shape, not generic advice.
Write it up as a new subsection in docs/plan/plan.md (pattern-match the existing "Per-Route Guards"
section: opt-in per route via fragment field, no SEAM-wide default) and add it as a phase or fold
into an existing one (natural fit: extends Phase 1's request-handling core). Should note the
interaction with the Credential Health Sentinel's probe traffic and with cost-governed routes
(x-cost-per-call) — a cache hit should not count against x-quota.

title: 1a.1.D: Add request validation with structured 400s and GET /docs/route pointer
description:
SEAM's stated differentiator (plan Overview + Architecture): a malformed request gets a structured 400 naming the bad field, the expected shape, and a pointer to /docs/route — not a bare 400. Validation runs against the served (hand-written whole) spec via pb33f/libopenapi-validator (ADR-001, already in go.mod).

Scope:
- Validate incoming caller requests against the served spec using libopenapi-validator.
- Structured 400 body: identifies the bad field/path, the expected shape, and includes a pointer to GET /docs/route?path=<template>&method=<m>&version=_unversioned. The route selector is a QUERY PARAMETER, not a path segment (plan: net/http + Traefik normalize encoded slashes, so /docs/{route} as a segment cannot survive).
- GET /docs/route?path=<openapi-path-template> with optional &method= and &version= on caller port -> that route's slice of the spec (parameters, request/response schemas, annotations in force, one worked example). Without &method= covers every method on that path. In 1a there is one contract (_unversioned); version-selection machinery is Phase 8 (bf-4c48). Pointers carry &version=_unversioned from 1a.

Fourth child of the 1a.1 split (parent bf-4ks); depends on bf-3ys4. Acceptance:
- A request violating the served spec -> 400 JSON naming the offending field + expected shape + a /docs/route?path=...&method=...&version=_unversioned pointer.
- GET /docs/route?path=<served-path> returns that route's parameters + schemas + a worked example; without &method= it covers all methods on the path.
- A valid request is not rejected by the validator (validation does not break the happy path at the validation layer — full proxy forwarding is later phases).
- go test green (include a malformed-request fixture + a /docs/route fixture); gofmt/vet/lint clean.

title: 2.5: Inbound request-body tee (maxReplayableRequestBytes)
description: Phase 2 (Credential Health Sentinel specifies the mechanism; assigned to Phase 2 - edges 2 -> 13 and 2 -> 12). Buffer the inbound body up to maxReplayableRequestBytes (default 1 MiB, INDEPENDENT knob - shares only a default with maxBufferedResponseBytes, tuning one never moves the other); tee upstream while streaming; discard when the response status is known; above the cap or unreplayable (request-side protocol upgrade, unbounded chunked with no declared length) the body streams through unbuffered and each consumer degrades per its own section. Build the buffer ONLY - the 401 retry is Phase 12's, the loop-hash canonicalization Phase 13's.

Tests: scrub property/fuzz at every byte offset and chunk size (a single missed boundary is a leaked credential), AND the log-capture test (Security Threat Matrix -> Audit logging): run the acceptance suite at max verbosity, grep every sink for each injected value, a hit fails the build.

title: 11.1: Per-origin circuit breaker + x-breaker + structured 503
description: Phase 11 (Passive Route Health owns the policy). Failure = transport faults (refused/reset, DNS, TLS handshake), timeouts, and 5xx ONLY - no 4xx ever counts, and a 401 NEVER counts (even one triggering refetch-retry); SEAM's own 400/429/500 never count. 5 consecutive -> open 30 s; half-open admits ONE real caller (no synthetic probe), any non-failure closes, re-failure re-opens with backoff 30/60/120 s capped at 5 min; keyed on resolved upstream origin (scheme+host+port; per x-upstream-map entry). Structured 503: upstream, openedAt, lastError, derived Retry-After (seconds remaining, floored at 1, body matches header). x-breaker {threshold, openSeconds, maxOpenSeconds, enabled} fragment-root + per-instance override; same-origin disagreement: lint fails the PR, runtime strictest values govern with the disagreement at /config/status; ON BY DEFAULT - enabled: false is the lint-flagged, enumerated opt-out.
